name: 1701 S. Prairie Avenue — the Hibbard stable by the tracks and its storey-and-a-half stable south of it (draft refined by T-3316 from the Chicagology photograph)

grade.why: Pictured: a picture on the Images tab shows it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 2.250, v -15.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.61 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1701 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1701 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: T-3316: the 1911 sheet's outline (sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_20.jpg, px x 4660-4950, y 3553-3936), read off the raster through the trace's own px-to-metre fit (0.0508 m a px) into this frame: the two-storey part r1 from the north wall (v 0) to the line at sheet y 3816 (v 13.25), 9.0 m across; the storey-and-a-half crossed stable r2 from there to the south wall (v 19.36), 11.6 m across, its west wall 2.4 m west of r1's. Both are parallelograms on the slant of the right-of-way: r1's west wall steps 0.277 m east a metre south and its east wall 0.304 (taken as one shear, 0.29: the corners within 0.2 m), r2's walls the same. The polygon is the two outlines' union. It replaces the draft's rectangle fit (70% of the main part).

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey brick building by the tracks, unlettered': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The sheet colours both parts pink, brick; the photograph shows brick walls.

parts.from: s20fp-1701-b2 p1: the sheet's '2' building by the tracks, on its own wall lines, sheared (T-3316)
s20fp-1701-b2 p2-p4: the sheet's crossed '1½' stable south of it, on its own wall lines, sheared (T-3316)

draft_plan.note: T-3316: the plan is the 1911 sheet's, no longer the rules' fit. r1, the '2' part, and r2, the crossed '1½' part, stand on the outlines the sheet draws, unsheared in this record (rect) and built sheared by skew_per_m 0.29: each metre south steps the walls 0.29 m east, so the north and south walls keep their line across the lot and the long walls take the right-of-way's slant. Storeys per part are the sheet's. r1's eave (4.5 m) and hip (20 degrees) and r2's eave (3.6 m, re-read 2026-11-03) are read off the Chicagology photograph through the house's camera; r2 is hipped (26 degrees) under the photograph's eave, its yard front carrying a narrow gable 1.8 m across at its north corner rather than a gable on the sheet's whole 6.1 m end: the photograph shows both slopes of that gable, its apex about 1.4 m south of the wing's corner (L-t3316-hibbard-1701-stable).

draft_elevation.note: T-3316: read off the Chicagology photograph of the Hibbard house (cgn-1701-hibbard-photo-wide, 1945 x 1207 px), whose right edge (x 1590-1945) shows the stable's yard (west) front 57-68 m off, through the house's own solved camera carried into this frame unchanged (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie_coach_house/chicagology_front.json), at about 35 px a metre. REGISTERED ON THE WING: through that camera the sheet puts the crossed stable's north-west corner at x 2035 px, where the photograph's gabled wing begins at x 1867, about 4 m north of the sheet's line along the wall; no camera fits the house and the wing both (a re-fit holding the wing leaves the house's corners 40-60 px out), so the features are placed by their offsets from the wing's corner, as the photograph shows them, and the difference is open in the match record. READ: a hipped slate roof on a bracketed cornice at about 4.5 m; a square lantern about 2.0 m across over the roof's north part, three round-headed lights a face, its cornice at about 8.6 m under a pyramidal cap to about 9.9 m and a finial; a wall gable with a curved head rising about 0.95 m over the cornice, an oculus in it, over a two-light window in a pale stone frame under a hood (top about 4.0 m); three round oculi about 1 m up the wall; two short capped stacks on the roof's south part; and the lower wing's yard front, eave about 3.6 m, carrying at its north corner a narrow straight-sided gable (about 1.8 m across, its apex about 0.95 m over the eave, both slopes seen; measured at about 47 px a metre on the wing's face with the whole stable's 167 px offset taken out), a lunette under its springing and an oculus under that, a pale band low on its wall (T-3316, re-read: the wing is hipped behind that gable, not gabled on its whole end). INVENTED: the carriage door in r1's yard front at its north end (behind the house in the picture; a stable's yard needs one, the sheet draws no drive); the lantern's place across the roof (one view gives x, not depth); the stacks' depth and heights; the faces the picture does not see (r1's north and east walls, r2's south and east) are blank or the rules' openings; colours (monochrome: brick per the sheet, slate). Liberty L-t3316-hibbard-1701-stable.

function.note: Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses a brick stable over the outline (its stable sign) and the 1911 sheet crosses the 1½-storey part X; the Chicagology photograph shows a lantern-ventilated hipped building with low oculi, a stable's. The 1911 sheet's '2-storey brick building by the tracks' is read as the house's stable for 1904. Inferred.

Hibbard residence.] Photograph of the front and south flank from the west side of Prairie Avenue; photographer and original holder not named. Reproduced by Chicagology, '1701 Prairie Avenue' (chicagology.com/chicagostreets/prairieavenue/1701prairie/); the same negative is reproduced in two halftones on the Glessner House Museum's blog.

the storeys' heights and the lights' places and sizes through its solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie/chicagology_front.json)
the cornice, the roof's deck and rail and the stack

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2335, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1933 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20 trace (s20fp-1701-b2), the T-1840 census (s20-1701-r1, s20-1701-r2) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20-032; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335). T-3316 (piece 2 of T-3310, a piece of T-1933) refines it in place on this builder, the K12 kit having no hipped roof or lantern: the plan on the 1911 sheet's parallelogram (both buildings' west and east walls on the slant of the Illinois Central right-of-way, 0.29 m east for every metre south, the draft builder's new skew_per_m), and the elevation read off the Chicagology photograph of the Hibbard house (cgn-1701-hibbard-photo-wide, source chicagology_1701_hibbard_photo), whose right edge shows the stable's yard front through the house's own solved camera (data/reference_views/hibbard_house_1701_prairie_coach_house/chicagology_front.json). The engraving of the house (a16-cgy-1701-hibbard-engraving) and the Glessner House rear halftone do not show it. The draft rules skip s20-1701-r1 and s20-1701-r2. Liberty L-t3316-hibbard-1701-stable.
